takeaways: The U.S.-Canada trade war is on — Washington imposed 50% tariffs on roughly $20B of Canadian goods after talks collapsed, and Canada is retaliating after Labor Day. Watch construction materials costs and a fresh inflation impulse just as the Fed weighs its next move.

A pivotal rates week: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh makes his Jackson Hole debut Thursday, with Nvidia earnings and July core PCE (forecast 3.3% y/y) both landing Wednesday — together they set the September rate path that governs the CRE refinancing window.

Senior housing deal flow keeps accelerating — experts now call for a record acquisition year, Berkadia just sold a 246-unit Jacksonville community, and Sonida landed a $380M Ally loan — even as an executive exodus at Fannie Mae injects new uncertainty into agency lending.

items.headline: U.S. slaps 50% tariffs on $20B of Canadian goods; trade war spirals
items.summary: After trade talks broke down, the U.S. imposed 50% tariffs on about $20 billion worth of Canadian goods, and Canada announced retaliatory post-Labor Day tariffs as the two countries spiral toward an all-out trade war. For developers and operators, tariffs on Canadian lumber, steel and aluminum threaten construction and renovation budgets and add a fresh inflation impulse ahead of the Fed's September meeting. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: Fannie Mae sheds a dozen senior executives, stoking mortgage-market worries
items.summary: Roughly a dozen high-ranking officials were let go at Fannie Mae in a single week, raising concerns about deeper turmoil at one of the firms backing major portions of the U.S. mortgage market. Instability at the agencies matters directly for multifamily and senior housing borrowers who rely on agency debt for acquisitions and refis. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: Warsh's Jackson Hole debut, Nvidia earnings and July PCE collide this week
items.summary: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivers his first Jackson Hole keynote Thursday, while Wednesday brings a data convergence: Nvidia's Q2 results after the close, July core PCE (forecast 3.3% y/y), revised Q2 GDP and durable goods. An in-line PCE print would further reduce rate-hike odds and firm up the fall financing window for CRE deals.

items.headline: Senior living dealbook: 246-unit Jacksonville community trades hands
items.summary: Berkadia sold Wyndham Lakes, a 246-unit IL/AL/memory care community in suburban Jacksonville, to Michigan-based Stagecoach Capital, which plans to expand the acuity mix — a notable Florida trade in Lloyd Jones's backyard. Berkadia also moved a 138-unit AL/MC community to JDI Realty (Evolve Senior Living to manage), and Blueprint closed a two-community, 96-unit memory care portfolio near Cleveland.

items.headline: Experts call for record senior living acquisition year; Sonida lands $380M
items.summary: With occupancy near 90%, construction starts thin and REIT/public buyers' share of acquisitions up to 32% from 24% in 2024, industry experts say 2026 could set a record for senior living and care acquisitions. Recent prints back it up: Sonida Senior Living secured a $380M loan from Ally Bank and a Lewes, Delaware community sold for $85.5M — liquidity is returning across the capital stack.

items.headline: Nvidia bets $6B on Poolside to build America's open-weight AI answer
items.summary: Nvidia is spending $6 billion with startup Poolside to build one of the world's most powerful open-weight AI models under its Nemotron project, aiming to rival both Chinese open models and U.S. frontier labs within a year. Cheaper, customizable open models would lower the cost of deploying AI in operations-heavy businesses like property management. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: Boomers are smoking more pot — and retirement communities are fuming
items.summary: Seniors are among the fastest-growing demographics for marijuana use, and rising cannabis use inside retirement communities is sparking conflicts with neighbors. For operators, it's a live policy question: smoke-free rules, designated areas, and state-law patchworks are becoming resident-relations issues, not hypotheticals. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: Senior living websites are still too static, sales leaders warn
items.summary: Senior Housing News reports that despite recent web upgrades, operators' sites remain too static for an increasingly web-savvy boomer customer — sales and marketing leaders are pushing toward interactive pricing tools, virtual tours and AI-driven personalization. Digital presence is becoming a real occupancy lever as the 80-plus wave arrives.

items.headline: The wild week Scott Bessent was schooled by the bond market
items.summary: The Treasury Department's bond buyback announcement stemmed a Treasury selloff — but not for long, as yields resumed climbing in a turbulent week for government debt. Long-end volatility feeds straight into CRE: benchmark rates, not just Fed policy, will decide where senior housing acquisition debt prices this fall. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: Inside Camp Kotok: Wall Street's wilderness retreat is spooked by AI
items.summary: At money manager David Kotok's invite-only Maine fishing retreat, financiers and policymakers spent the weekend voicing peak anxiety about the AI trade — questioning the hype while continuing to pour money in. With Nvidia reporting Wednesday, the paradox captures the market's biggest single-stock risk. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: Proptech consolidation: Dwelly raises ~$93M, makes 7th acquisition of 2026
items.summary: UK proptech Dwelly raised roughly $93M in blended equity and debt from General Catalyst, Begin Capital, S16VC and Trinity Capital to roll up independent letting agencies, announcing its seventh acquisition of the year, while Giraffe360 closed a $10M Series B. Investors are betting AI automation will compress agency margins — property shares are already reacting.

items.headline: Jack Daniel's heirs fight to keep control amid $15B hostile bid
items.summary: Brown-Forman's founding family — in control for 150+ years — is split over how to respond to a $15 billion hostile takeover bid as profits shrink, shares sit 60% below their five-year high and the CEO heads for the exit. A case study in how family-controlled companies handle succession, governance and unsolicited capital. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: British grads skip top colleges for white-collar apprenticeships
items.summary: British high-school graduates are increasingly bypassing university for white-collar apprenticeships, questioning the value of a degree in a job market reshaped by AI. A leading indicator for U.S. talent pipelines: employers that build earn-while-you-learn tracks may win the next generation of operations and site-level talent. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: Moderna surges 177% on melanoma vaccine breakthrough
items.summary: Moderna and Merck's personalized mRNA melanoma vaccine posted successful late-stage trial results, vaulting Moderna's market value from about $25 billion to roughly $60 billion in a week. Beyond the market story, targeted mRNA cancer therapy arriving this decade has real implications for senior health and longevity. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: Boards and CEOs are sharply divided on who owns AI
items.summary: IMD's 2026 leadership research finds boards, CEOs and executives split on who should own AI strategy, arguing the winning organizations won't be those with the most polished strategies but the ones that learn fastest when strategies break. Clear AI ownership is becoming a governance question, not just an IT one.

items.headline: AI's hunger for training data puts rare-book dealers in a bind
items.summary: Used-book sellers worldwide have traced waves of mysterious bulk orders — hundreds of books at a time, no haggling — to AI companies' need for fresh LLM training content, with many volumes ending up sliced, scanned and destroyed. Dealers worry irreplaceable books are being 'sent to the guillotine.' (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: The secret's out on the Catskills real estate boom
items.summary: NYC buyers priced out of the Hudson Valley have pushed north and west into the Catskills, fueling multimillion-dollar renovations and new construction, with revamped farmhouses selling at once unheard-of prices. Another data point in the migration of urban wealth toward lifestyle markets. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: Chasing total solar eclipses is strangely addictive
items.summary: WSJ's Pamela Paul, hooked since 2017, joined eclipse chasers from around the world on cliffs outside León, Spain for this month's totality — birds hush, dogs bark, grown adults weep. A reminder that awe is a bucket-list amenity money can still buy. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: Could you beat a high-schooler on the new AP personal-finance test?
items.summary: More than half of U.S. states now require a stand-alone personal-finance course to graduate, and the College Board is rolling out a new AP Business with Personal Finance course this school year. WSJ shares sample questions so you can test yourself against the teenagers. (via WSJ 10-Point)
